title: Address spoofing, ARP poisoning and DNS poisoning

videos.script: Every packet says where it came from. The sender writes that field, and nothing checks it. {{claim}} In this lesson a machine on the internet sends a request claiming to come from the company's own servers, and the shop receives it. {{forged}} Then the firewall learns to ask a simple question. Could this source really have arrived on this interface? Two rules, and the forged request never gets past the edge. Pointed the other way, the same check stops the company's own machines from sending forged packets out. {{edge}} Then DNS. A resolver's cache can be poisoned with an answer nobody sent. You will ask a signed zone for an answer, change it without signing it again, and watch a validating resolver refuse to believe it. {{dnssec}}
